llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (A/B test analysis) matches the requested footprint: it is instruction-only, asks for no credentials, and its instructions stay within the stated domain — but provenance is missing and the package metadata/version mismatch is a minor incoherence to investigate.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (A/B test analysis) align with the content: SKILL.md describes importing CSVs, running analyses, and generating reports. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains only usage docs and example commands that operate on a local CSV and produce a report; it does not instruct reading unrelated system files or exfiltrating data. Note: the document is instructional only and references running 'openclaw run ab-test-analyzer', but no implementation or install is included in the package — confirm where the actual analysis runs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are included, which minimizes install-time risk. Because this is instruction-only, nothing is written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That is proportional for a CSV-based analysis tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no 'always' privilege or other elevated persistence requested. The skill is user-invocable and allows normal autonomous invocation by the agent (platform default).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its A/B analysis purpose and requests no credentials, but note it contains only documentation (no code or install). Before installing/using: 1) Ask the publisher for the implementation/source or a trusted registry URL — provenance is missing. 2) Verify which runtime will actually perform the analysis (local vs remote). 3) Avoid uploading sensitive or PII-containing CSVs until you confirm where data is processed/stored. 4) Resolve the small metadata mismatch (skill.json lists version 1.0.0 while registry shows 1.0.34) — it could be benign but is worth confirming.
